Kindia, the zoo’s 20-year-old pygmy hippo, started showing signs of labor at around 8.15am last Sunday, it said. Around four hours later, the calf’s feet emerged and after 1.5 hours of active labor, Kindia successfully gave birth to the baby pygmy hippo.

rfi.title: French unemployment hits six-year high as jobless total reaches 2.7 million
rfi.description: The number of unemployed people in France rose to 2.7 million in the second quarter of 2026, pushing the jobless rate to its highest level in nearly six years, according to the national statistics agency Insee.

rfi.title: 'People at war have come to help': Ukrainian firefighters battle French wildfire
rfi.description: A team of 70 firefighters from Ukraine is on deployment in southwest France, where wildfires have scorched 42,000 hectares in the worst blaze in decades. RFI met the Ukrainian rescuers helping to put out the last of the flames.

rfi.title: Ceuta and Western Sahara at heart of US-Morocco rapprochement
rfi.description: Since late July, the United States has been increasingly signalling a move to strengthen its ties with Morocco, both economically and diplomatically. In 2020, the US backed Morocco’s autonomy plan for Western Sahara in exchange for the country normalising relations with Israel. Now, Washington appears ready to support Morocco’s claims regarding the Spanish enclaves of Ceuta and Melilla.

rfi.title: Fifa executives rally behind Infantino despite commercial plan fiasco
rfi.description: Gianni Infantino’s position as world football’s most powerful administrator appeared more secure on Thursday after senior Fifa executives backed him to remain president despite his failed attempt to overhaul the commercial operations behind competitions including the World Cup.

rfi.title: Russia accuses France of ‘silencing dissent’ over journalist expulsion
rfi.description: Russia has accused France of suppressing freedom of expression, after French authorities ordered the expulsion of pro-Kremlin Russian journalist Xenia Fedorova and froze her assets.

rfi.title: Le Court Pienaar wins stage six of Women's Tour de France as Reusser keeps lead
rfi.description: Kimberley Le Court Pienaar claimed stage six of the Tour de France Femmes, as Marlen Reusser took her slender lead over Demi Vollering into Friday's seventh stage.

rfi.title: Ebola cases near 4,000 as DRC struggles to contain fast-spreading outbreak
rfi.description: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic ⁠of Congo is spreading faster than efforts to fight it, the head of the World Health Organization has warned, with nearly 4,000 confirmed cases so far. With five provinces known to be affected, authorities in Kinshasa are concerned about the deadly virus reaching the capital.

rfi.title: Ghana and Mali battle for place in last eight at Women's Africa Cup of Nations
rfi.description: Ghana and Mali fight for a place on Thursday in a last-eight showdown with tournament debutants Malawi. Both sides go into the Group D clash at the Stade Rachid Moulay in Casablanca aiming to reach the quarter-finals for the second tournament on the trot.

rfi.title: Threats by Corsican separatist group FLNC-UC trigger anti-terrorism inquiry
rfi.description: A masked appearance by armed Corsican separatists and threats made against people moving to the island from mainland France has reignited tensions over the Mediterranean island’s political future, amid growing concerns about intimidation and violence.

rfi.title: New Caledonia races to avoid shutdown as new government takes office
rfi.description: New Caledonia’s 19th government formally took office on Wednesday after its 11 members unanimously agreed on the allocation of portfolios, with the immediate task of securing €109 million by the end of August to avoid a complete shutdown of the local administration.

rfi.title: Why has Ukraine's former military chief given up on NATO membership?
rfi.description: The former chief of Ukraine's armed forces, Valery Zaluzhny, says his country, fighting Russian invasion since 2022, will "never" join NATO – despite Kyiv's intention to become a member of the military alliance. While some analysts suggest Zaluzhny is primarily seeking to highlight the alliance’s weaknesses, others say he is laying the groundwork for a presidential bid.

rfi.title: Ex-French PM Attal targeted by Russian 'interference' ahead of 2027 vote
rfi.description: Gabriel Attal, France’s former prime minister and Renaissance party leader, has been targeted by “foreign interference originating in Russia”, in the latest in a series of Kremlin‑linked operations aimed at destabilising the 2027 presidential election.

rfi.title: Jordan warns status quo in Jerusalem 'under threat' as ministers meet in Amman
rfi.description: Amman hosted an emergency ministerial meeting on Wednesday to rally support behind Jordan’s custodianship of Jerusalem’s holy sites, as Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi warned that Israeli measures risk igniting a wider religious conflict.

rfi.title: France welcomes Algeria’s arrest of alleged DZ Mafia crime boss
rfi.description: France's Minister of Justice, Gérald Darmanin has hailed Algerian security services for their work in the arrest of an alleged key figure in Marseille's crime world.

rfi.title: July France's hottest month since records began, says national weather service
rfi.description: July this year was the hottest month in France since records began in 1900, according to meteorologists. It was also France's third-driest July, with rainfall nearly 70 percent below average.

rfi.title: Ile-de-France region files suit for compensation over Fontainebleau forest fire
rfi.description: The Ile-de-France regional council this week launched a civil law suit over the recent wildfire which decimated more than 2,000 hectares of the Fontainebleau forest, south of Paris. A criminal investigation has been opened into the blaze, which the national forestry office says caused significant environmental damage.

rfi.title: Kremlin critic leaves Moscow for Paris after ban from running for election
rfi.description: Russian anti-war politician Boris Nadezhdin has left the country after being prevented from standing in September’s parliamentary elections, becoming the latest prominent Kremlin critic to move abroad amid an intensifying crackdown on dissent.

rfi.title: France announces further investment to combat drug trafficking in Guiana
rfi.description: France's Minister for Public Accounts outlined on Monday a slew of measures designed to combat drug trafficking in the Caribbean territory of French Guiana, one of the world's major hubs for smugglers.

euronews.title: Spanish police dismantle major Mediterranean migrant and drugs smuggling network
euronews.description: Investigators believe the group was responsible for at least 64 migrant smuggling operations in which more than 2,000 people were brought to Spain, generating profits of more than €24 million.

euronews.title: EU sanctions five people linked to Russia’s military industry after Ukraine strikes
euronews.description: The EU sanctioned five individuals tied to Russia’s military-industrial complex after recent Russian air strikes on Ukraine, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said, accusing Moscow of escalating attacks on civilians as its forces stalled.

euronews.title: Uzbekistan-developed AI module launches aboard Earth observation satellite
euronews.description: The Samarkand-2028 Earth observation satellite has entered orbit carrying an AI module developed by Uzbek engineers, processing data in orbit before transmission to improve efficiency in fields including agriculture and environmental monitoring.

euronews.title: Surprise discovery as ancient domus uncovered beneath restoration site in Rome
euronews.description: A routine restoration project on Rome's Caelian Hill has led to the discovery of an ancient Roman building decorated with mosaics, frescoes and painted ceilings. Archaeologists have uncovered eight rooms dating back to the second century AD.

euronews.title: Danube: Wehrmacht soldiers and WWII motorbike recovered after 80 years
euronews.description: The Danube is at such a low level that Second World War relics are resurfacing in Budapest: alongside a motorbike, the bodies of two soldiers have been recovered.

euronews.description: The growing number of specimens along the Cantabrian coast has forced swimming bans on several Basque beaches and prompted health authorities to step up guidance on how to respond to stings.

euronews.title: New EU AI transparency rules apply to everyday users too, not just Big Tech
euronews.description: The EU's AI Act has largely been associated with strict obligations for high-risk systems and big tech companies. From this month, that changes, as sweeping new transparency rules widen the net far beyond corporations to catch individual creators, freelancers and everyday users, too.

euronews.title: Sri Lanka deploys troops to contain growing prison unrest, minister says
euronews.description: Officials have attributed the growing unrest to acute overcrowding. Sri Lanka's prisons hold about four times their intended capacity.

euronews.title: Russia might use fake Ukrainian drones to target Baltic infrastructure, Lithuania warns
euronews.description: Moscow could use recovered Ukrainian drone parts to stage an attack on Baltic infrastructure in a bid to undermine NATO support for Kyiv, Lithuania’s defence minister said.

lemonde.description: L’irruption dans l’enclave espagnole de 72 000 personnes venues du Maroc, entre le 30 et le 31 juillet, a mis en lumière les fêlures et les solidarités qui traversent cette ville où coexistent depuis des siècles chrétiens et musulmans.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, incendies : « La Gironde est meurtrie mais elle est debout », déclare le ministre du tourisme

lemonde.title: Au Cap-Ferret, Benoît Bartherotte, maître en son royaume
lemonde.description: Lors du grand incendie qui a frappé la Gironde, le volcanique patriarche de 79 ans a refusé d’évacuer la presqu’île du bassin d’Arcachon et a édifié de son propre chef un pare-feu. Une attitude bien dans ses habitudes : depuis quarante ans, l’ex-homme d’affaires construit une digue controversée pour préserver la langue de sable des assauts de l’océan.

lemonde.title: Au Mexique, l’armée étend son empire économique, des chemins de fer aux hôtels en passant par les aéroports
lemonde.description: La gauche au pouvoir confie, depuis quelques années, la construction et la gestion de multiples infrastructures et activités à l’institution militaire, arguant notamment de son efficacité. A l’exception de celui des forces armées cubaines, le patrimoine de l’armée mexicaine est désormais sans équivalent en Amérique latine.

lemonde.description: Il avait consacré sa vie à réveiller la mémoire des juifs dans le pays balte, créant notamment un musée à Riga. Il s’est éteint le 30 juillet.

Afrique du Sud : des usines en manque de main d'œuvre après le départ des migrants
france24fr.description: 🇿🇦 En Afrique du Sud, plusieurs usines sont actuellement à l'arrêt après le départ de nombreux migrants, sur fond de semaines de manifestations visant les étrangers. Cette situation entraîne des pénuries de main-d'œuvre et laisse de nombreux postes vacants.

france24fr.title: À Cuba, la survie au quotidien de la population face à la crise énergétique
france24fr.description: À Cuba, la crise énergétique se double d'un effondrement économique sans précédent, alors que Washington multiplie les sanctions. Entre pression américaine et crise intérieure, la population tente de tenir, jour après jour. Reportage à La Havane.

france24fr.title: En images : quand les fleuves européens s'assèchent, les vestiges du passé refont surface
france24fr.description: Alors que la sécheresse s'abat sur l'Europe depuis de longues semaines, les grands fleuves européens se retirent et laissent apparaître des vestiges d'un autre temps. Navires de la Seconde Guerre mondiale, mammouth,... : tour d'horizon en images  de ces découvertes.

france24fr.title: Thaïlande : un adolescent tue huit personnes dans un lycée près de Bangkok
france24fr.description: Un adolescent thaïlandais a tué vendredi huit personnes dont deux de ses grands-parents, avant de se donner la mort dans un établissement scolaire situé dans la banlieue de Bangkok. La détention d’armes à feu et la violence armée sont relativement répandues en Thaïlande, qui a connu plusieurs fusillades meurtrières au cours des six dernières années, avec des enfants parmi les victimes. Récit d'Axelle Simon.

france24fr.title: Colombie : le président d'extrême droite promet la rupture
france24fr.description: En Colombie, le président élu le 21 juin dernier, l’avocat millionnaire d’ultradroite Abelardo de la Espriella, prend officiellement ses fonctions ce vendredi. Cette investiture ne se déroule pas dans la capitale, Bogota, mais à Cali, troisième ville du pays. Un symbole pour le président élu, puisque la ville est l’un des bastions des groupes armés engagés dans le narcotrafic. Récit de Romain Michelot.

france24fr.title: Ukraine - Russie : nouvelles frappes de part et d’autre
france24fr.description: L’Ukraine intensifie ses attaques de drones sur le territoire russe, en visant notamment des centres logistiques. Un nouvel incendie s’est déclaré vendredi 7 août dans un entrepôt à Ekaterinbourg, dans l’Oural, après la chute de trois drones sur le toit du site. Correspondance d'Emmanuelle Chaze depuis Kharkiv pour France 24.

france24fr.title: Argentine : mobilisation et heurts contre un projet de loi de Milei
france24fr.description: En Argentine, les manifestations contre le projet de loi de Javier Milei sur la propriété privée se poursuivent et se durcissent. Dans la capitale, Buenos Aires, des heurts ont eu lieu entre la police et des manifestants alors que le projet de loi était examiné au Sénat. Il prévoit notamment de faciliter les expulsions de terres et s’inscrit dans la politique ultralibérale du gouvernement Milei. Explications de Romain Michelot.

france24fr.title: Afghanistan : la renaissance des footballeuses de l'équipe des réfugiées
france24fr.description: Créée il y a un an, l'équipe de football des réfugiées afghanes poursuit son développement. Les joueuses se sont retrouvées en Nouvelle-Zélande pour s'entraîner à plus de 13 000 km de leur pays. Une renaissance pour ces femmes, cinq ans après la prise de pouvoir par les talibans en Afghanistan. Récit d'Alice Brogat.

france24fr.title: France : face aux chaleurs extrêmes, les vendanges commencent déjà
france24fr.description: Après plusieurs épisodes de canicule et de sécheresses à répétition, les vendanges débutent avec plusieurs semaines d’avance dans certaines régions françaises. Pour en parler, l'invité de France 24 est Simon Le Berre, membre de la commission viticole de la Confédération paysanne nationale.

france24fr.title: Cisjordanie occupée : le casse-tête quotidien des ambulanciers
france24fr.description: Routes bloquées, checkpoints fermés, déplacements ralentis : après chaque nouvel épisode de violence, les restrictions de circulation se renforcent en Cisjordanie occupée. Notre correspondante Claire Duhamel a suivi un ambulancier confronté quotidiennement aux barrages et aux détours dans ce territoire verrouillé par Israël.

france24fr.title: Le "zoo humain" d'Anvers : la Belgique fait face à la déshumanisation coloniale
france24fr.description: En 1894, alors qu'a lieu à Anvers une exposition universelle, la Belgique fait expédier par bateau 144 Congolais pour les exhiber dans le pavillon Congo en plein cœur de la ville. Dans ce "zoo humain", sept Congolais finissent par décéder de maladies. Aujourd'hui, cette terrible histoire hante toujours la Belgique comme l'une des pages les plus sombres de son histoire coloniale.

france24fr.title: "Sauvez mon petit !" : l'accueil des enfants espagnols en France pendant la guerre civile (2/4)
france24fr.description: Il y a 90 ans, la guerre d'Espagne (2/4). Au cours de ce conflit, près de 15 000 enfants originaires de la zone républicaine ont été envoyés en France. Ces "enfants de la guerre" ont été placés dans des familles d'accueil ou dans des colonies créées pour eux. Un ouvrage lève aujourd'hui le voile sur cette opération humanitaire méconnue.

france24fr.title: Yan Diomandé, l'Ivoirien qui affole les records en rejoignant le Real Madrid
france24fr.description: Le Real Madrid a officialisé la signature de Yan Diomandé jusqu'en 2033 en provenance de Leipzig. Estimé à 125 millions d’euros, plus 15 millions de bonus, le transfert devient le plus cher de l'histoire du club madrilène. À seulement 19 ans, l'international ivoirien devient également le joueur africain le plus cher de l’histoire.

france24fr.title: Moyen-Orient en direct : Arabie saoudite, Pakistan et Turquie signent un accord de défense mutuelle
france24fr.description: Le prince héritier saoudien, Mohamed ben Salmane, réunit à Jeddah les dirigeants turc et pakistanais ont scellé, avec un accord de défense mutuelle, leur rapprochement opéré sur fond de guerre au Moyen-Orient. france24fr.title: Au Nouveau-Mexique, Meta devra verser 567 millions de dollars pour protéger les mineurs

spiegel.description: Der Irankrieg leert die US-Arsenale. Es dürfte Jahre dauern, bis sie wieder auf Vorkriegsniveau sind. Doch Donald Trump will das nicht wahrhaben – und ist wütend auf einen seiner treuesten Jünger.

spiegel.title: Berlin – Stromausfall: Stadt zahlt 900.000 Euro an Hotelkosten
spiegel.description: Zehntausende Berliner Haushalte waren während des großflächigen Stromausfalls im Januar ohne Strom. Die Folgen sind bis heute zu spüren, vor allem politisch. Aber auch auf den Konten der Betroffenen.

spiegel.title: Großbritannien: 97-jährige Betty Bromage bricht Wingwalking-Weltrekord
spiegel.description: Festgeschnallt auf einem Doppeldecker dreht sie Loopings am Himmel: Betty Bromage ist ehemalige Schlaganfallpatientin und erneut Inhaberin des Weltrekords im »Wingwalking«. Warum macht die Britin das?

spiegel.title: Christian Stocker: Kanzler gerät wegen Aussage zu Care-Arbeit unter Druck
spiegel.description: Die Debatte über gerechte Verteilung und Entlohnung von Care-Arbeit hat ÖVP-Mann Christian Stocker als »Materialisierung von Kindern« abgetan. Nach heftiger Kritik rudert der 66-Jährige jetzt zurück.

spiegel.title: Südkorea: Verband soll Schiedsrichtern Besuche in Massagesalons finanziert haben
spiegel.description: Seit der verkorksten WM kommt der Fußballverband Südkoreas nicht zur Ruhe. Laut Medienberichten soll die KFA Referees Besuche in speziellen Massagesalons bezahlt haben – auch vor einem entscheidenden WM-Qualifikationsspiel.

spiegel.title: Lina E.: Bundesgerichtshof bestätigt Beugehaft für verurteilte Linksextremistin
spiegel.description: Sie war von 2018 bis 2020 an mehreren teils lebensgefährlichen Angriffen auf tatsächliche und vermeintliche Anhänger der rechten Szene beteiligt. Ihre Strafe hat Lina E. bereits verbüßt. Doch jetzt sitzt sie wieder ein.

spiegel.title: Frankreich: Wie die »Grande Épicerie« den Foodie noch überraschen kann
spiegel.description: Franzosen erheben die Nahrungsaufnahme bekanntermaßen zum Großereignis. In der Pariser »Grande Épicerie« wird aber noch der verwöhnteste Foodie-Touri überrascht.

spiegel.title: Sonnenfinsternis in Spanien: Licht aus - und die Urlauber kommen
spiegel.description: Noch nicht einmal für zwei Minuten wird es in Spanien dunkel, doch für das Himmelspektakel reisen Fans aus der ganzen Welt an. Die Region Kastilien und Léon hofft auf nachhaltige Faszination.

spiegel.title: »Gilmore Girls«: US-Serie bekommt eigene Dokumentation – mit Blick hinter die Kulissen
spiegel.description: Passend zum 25. Jubiläum soll die US-Serie »Gilmore Girls« ein Comeback feiern. Eine Dokumentation, die vielversprechende Einblicke in die Geschichte hinter der Erfolgsserie verspricht. Was bisher bekannt ist.

spiegel.title: Amanda Knox: Schwester von Meredith Kercher kritisiert Comedy-Show
spiegel.description: »Über eine solche Comedyshow würde sie niemals lachen«: Die Schwester der 2007 ermordeten Meredith Kercher ist empört darüber, dass die ehemalige Tatverdächtige Amanda Knox Profit aus dem Fall schlägt.

spiegel.title: E-Scooter: Mehr Hirnverletzungen als auf Motorrad und Rad
spiegel.description: Die Unfallgefahr durch E-Scooter ist bekannt. Eine neue Untersuchung zeigt nun, wie viel gefährlicher die Fahrzeuge im Vergleich sind. Frauen und Kinder sind demnach besonders betroffen.

spiegel.title: »Harry Potter«: Rupert Grint berichtet über Coronazeit mit einer Neugeborenen
spiegel.description: Während der Coronapandemie wurden Rupert Grint und seine Partnerin Georgia Groome erstmals Eltern. Eine herausfordernde Zeit, sagt er heute, sogar traumatisch sei sie gewesen. Aber auch wunderschön.

spiegel.title: Rendsburg in Schleswig-Holstein: Spaziergänger findet Königspython am Kanalufer
spiegel.description: Eigentlich lebt der Königspython in West- und Zentralafrika. Nun wurde in ungewohntem Terrain ein Exemplar entdeckt. Die schleswig-holsteinische Polizei ermittelt.

spiegel.title: Luisa Neubauer und Sepp Müller (CDU): Wie können sich Klimaschutz und Wirtschaft vertragen?
spiegel.description: Der CDU-Politiker Sepp Müller sorgt sich um die Wettbewerbsfähigkeit der deutschen Wirtschaft, Aktivistin Luisa Neubauer um das Klima. Hier fechten sie den Streit aus. Und nähern sich an.

spiegel.title: Nachrichtenmüdigkeit: Warum wir auf lösungsorientierten Journalismus setzen
spiegel.description: Die deutsche Gesellschaft steckt im Stimmungstief, die Demokratie gilt als gefährdet. Sind daran auch Journalisten schuld? Wir versuchen etwas Neues.

spiegel.title: DR Kongo: Mehr als 4000 Menschen mit Ebola infiziert
spiegel.description: Der aktuelle Ebolaausbruch gilt als zweitgrößter weltweit: In der DR Kongo haben die Zahlen der Infizierten erstmals die Marke von 4000 überschritten. Experten befürchten nun eine Mutation.

spiegel.title: Schwimm-EM: Isabel Gose holt Gold im Freiwasser-Knockoutsprint
spiegel.description: Es gibt wieder Ärger wegen der Wasserqualität in der Seine. Isabel Gose zieht trotzdem durch und gewinnt ihr erstes Einzel-Gold im Freiwasser.

observador.title: Irão estará a preparar-se para a morte de Mojtaba Khamenei
observador.description: O IranWire diz que M. Khamenei está num estado "extremamente crítico" e por isso a morte do líder supremo do Irão não será vista como supresa. Ainda, o pedido pouco habitual de Ted Cruz a Trump.

observador.title: Modelo de IA da Meta invadiu sistema de outra empresa
observador.description: Uma "configuração incorreta" durante os testes de cibersegurança levaram a IA da Meta a desobedecer a instruções humanas. Modelos da Open AI, Anthropic e ChatGPT também realizaram "ações autónomas".

observador.title: Trabalhadores da Saúde no Algarve fazem greve
observador.description: Profissionais a fazer 16 horas consecutivas de trabalho são uma realidade e a ação é necessária para garantir um SNS "público, acessível e de qualidade", Rosa Franco, do Sindicato dos Trabalhadores.

observador.title: I Liga 2026/27 arranca com Estoril Praia-Famalicão
observador.description: Os estorilistas, a jogarem em casa, procuram contrariar a recente supremacia famalicense. Nos últimos quatro jogos, o Famalicão venceu todos os confrontos.

observador.title: Vendas de cerveja sobem 1,67% impulsionadas pelas sem ácool
observador.description: Uma em cada 12 cervejas consumidas na União Europeia é sem álcool. Portugal acompanha a tendência, com um aumento de cerca de 12% nas vendas no primeiro semestre de 2026.

observador.title: Amarante vai candidatar-se a Capital Portuguesa da Cultura
observador.description: Com o tem "o lugar do génio e o génio do lugar", Amarante — reconhecida pela UNESCO como Cidade Criativa da Música — disputa o título com Guarda, Leiria, Óbidos e Setúbal.

observador.title: O que esperar do eclipse que está a parar o país? — Debate
observador.description: Quarta feira, dia 12, vamos estar atentos ao céu para um fenómeno que não acontecia desde 1912, mas não será o único. Haverá ainda alinhamento de planetas ao amanhecer e uma chuva de meteoritos

observador.title: Espanha dá ultimato a Itália por controlos na fronteira
observador.description: Em causa estão os controlos levantados por Itália após o fluxo maciço de migrantes que entraram em Ceuta. O Governo de Madrid estipula um prazo para levantamento da situação, por Roma: domingo.

observador.title: Trump: há escassez de armas mas munições suficientes
observador.description: Com algumas munições "mais restritas", os EUA têm "um fornecimento ilimitado", assegurou Trump. Fabricantes vão aumentar a produção de mísseis Tomahawk e de projéteis para os sistemas Patriot.

observador.title: Tutora de crianças detida por violência doméstica
observador.description: Uma mulher de 51 anos, responsável por duas crianças de cinco e 10 anos, terá exercido violência física e psicológica sobre os menores: a GNR verificou "insalubridade" e falta de higiene na habitação.

observador.title: Quatro licenciaturas para um mundo de oportunidades
observador.description: Bioengenharia, Microbiologia, Nutrição e Ciências e Sociedade unem ciência, tecnologia, inovação e ligação ao mercado de trabalho. As candidaturas estão abertas.

observador.title: RTP: 80% dos trabalhadores não recebem subsídios polémicos
observador.description: Sindicatos e Comissão de Trabalhadores da RTP esclarecem que a maioria dos funcionários não recebe os subsídios sinalizados pela IGF como irregulares e preparam providência cautelar.

observador.title: As notícias das 12h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Etna: alerta máximo e voos desviados de Catânia
observador.description: Três voos desviados e chegadas IFR temporariamente suspensas. É mais um episódio eruptivo na cratera Voragine, num verão marcado por sucessivas erupções.

observador.title: Avanço rápido em campos de deslocados no Congo
observador.description: Pelo menos cinco dos 69 campos para pessoas deslocadas na RDCongo registaram casos de contágio, com 19 pessoas com Ébola, e cinco mortes. A taxa de rastreamento de contacto é de 77,7%.

observador.title: Suspeito de ameaças de morte em Amarante em preventiva
observador.description: O homem é suspeito de exercer "reiteradas" ameaças de morte contra a vítima, a sua companheira de 61 anos. As ameaças aconteceriam de "forma contínua".

observador.title: MP cabo-verdiano acusa ex-coordenador estatal de dois crimes
observador.description: Sandeney Fernandes é acusado de um crime de abuso de informação privilegiada. O processo está ligado à oferta pública de venda de 27,44% das ações da Caixa Económica, que são detidas pelo Estado.

observador.title: enegal anuncia ter plano para mediar crise política
observador.description: Decisão tomada em cimeira em Freetown. Plano será executado em fases até às eleições de 6 de dezembro — num país suspenso da CEDEAO, da UA e da CPLP.

nyt.title: How the Reflecting Pool Came to Mirror Trump’s Washington
nyt.description: A hospitality manager for the Trump Organization traveled to Las Vegas to find a solution to problems at a national landmark. This is the untold back story of the fallout.

nyt.title: Judge Dismisses Former Olympian’s Felony Charge in Reflecting Pool Case
nyt.description: The move ends the criminal case for David Hearn, a former Olympic canoeist, after prosecutors acknowledged that the Trump administration’s claims of vandalism were false.

nyt.title: Trump Targets Birthright Citizenship Again, and Activists Describe Abuse in Israeli Custody
Abdul El-Sayed Talks About His Victory, Chuck Schumer and His Mom
nyt.description: In an interview with The New York Times, Dr. El-Sayed recalled some of his conversations with establishment figures who once opposed his candidacy.

nyt.title: Candidate Field Set After Republicans Redrew Tennessee District Lines
nyt.description: Tennessee’s primary elections on Thursday came after Republican legislators carved up the state’s only majority-Black district in a bid to win all nine of the state’s House seats.

nyt.title: Blackburn Wins Republican Nomination for Tennessee Governor
nyt.description: Senator Marsha Blackburn easily beat two Republican rivals and is now favored to become the state’s first female governor after the November elections.

nyt.title: Seized on Their Way to Gaza, Activists Tell of Abuse in Israeli Custody
nyt.description: In interviews, more than 20 people who tried to break an Israeli blockade described beatings, electric shocks and other abuse after being captured. Israel denied the accusations.

nyt.title: The State of Iran’s Three Key Nuclear Sites
nyt.description: The conflict may have slowed, but not stopped, Iran’s nuclear program, officials and experts said.

nyt.title: The Gospel According to Anthony Bourdain
nyt.description: Fans of the late writer and chef are cultlike in their devotion. But have they misunderstood his message?

nyt.title: ‘Tony’ Review: An Appetite for Experiences
nyt.description: On 1970s Cape Cod, a young Anthony Bourdain chases love and finds his future in this rambunctious, utterly charming little movie.

nyt.title: Twin Falls Embraces Man Who Confronted Idaho In-N-Out Shooting
nyt.description: While the motive in the strip mall shooting rampage in Twin Falls, Idaho, remains elusive, a community embraces a bystander who stepped in.

nyt.title: Meta Ordered to Pay $567 Million Fine by New Mexico Judge
nyt.description: The penalty, imposed by a state judge, is on top of a $375 million fine ordered by a jury that found Meta misled users about the safety of its platforms.

nyt.title: Drought and Aging Pipes Plunge Puerto Rico Into Another Water Crisis
nyt.description: The disaster has put yet another spotlight on the government’s inability to provide basic services, deepening frustration among residents already plagued by regular power outages.

nyt.title: Luigi Mangione Is Facing Two Trials. Isn’t That Double Jeopardy?
nyt.description: The legal principle prevents a person from being tried twice for the same crime. But Mr. Mangione’s situation shows how complicated the judicial system can be.

nyt.title: Residents of London’s Barbican Are Battling a New Tower
nyt.description: The Barbican, a once divisive housing complex in central London, is now considered an architectural masterpiece. Residents are fighting plans for a 20-story building next door.

nyt.title: A Generation on Antidepressants Searches for the Exit
nyt.description: Many people feel that antidepressants block their true emotions, but they don’t have guidance about how to get off these drugs.

nyt.title: What Black Voters in Georgia Want and Aren’t Getting
nyt.description: In Georgia, where Black voters could help decide control of the Senate, Mara Gay asks what they want from America and the Democratic Party.

npr.title: Trump targets birthright citizenship. And, Iran aims to ban U.S. from Strait of Hormuz
npr.description: President Trump says he has signed two new orders targeting birthright citizenship. And, Iran is aiming to ban U.S. ships from the Strait of Hormuz.

npr.title: Besieged Sudanese city faces relentless drone strikes and risk of mass atrocities, U.N. warns
npr.description: Hundreds of thousands of civilians in el-Obeid are being battered by relentless drone strikes and face critical water shortages and a worsening cholera outbreak, while women and girls are reporting high rates of sexual violence.

npr.title: Student kills at least 6 in a shooting at a high school in Thailand, authorities say
npr.description: Authorities said the motive was still being investigated.

npr.title: Iran aims to ban U.S. and Israeli ships from Strait of Hormuz and charge others a toll
npr.description: Iran's parliament is reviewing a plan to ban ships linked to the U.S., Israel and other "hostile countries" from transiting the Strait of Hormuz. The Trump administration has rejected the plan.

npr.title: What is the best way to tackle poverty in Ethiopia? This new study tries cash, therapy, and more.
npr.description: A new study is out that looked at various ways to try to tackle poverty in Ethiopia. Turns out, cash helps, but the impact of therapy is less clear.

npr.title: Greetings from a wildlife park in central Sri Lanka that's a haven for elephants
npr.description: At a time of increased conflict between elephants and humans, as elephant habitats are converted to intensive agriculture, the Hurulu Eco Park is a place where the animals can graze unimpeded.

npr.title: This country is the latest to hit the elusive 95/95/95 HIV target
npr.description: The United Nations has set a goal for near universal HIV diagnosis and treatment for all by 2030. No country in Asia has hit the mark — until this year.

npr.title: Gianni Infantino gets internal support at crisis meeting to remain as FIFA president
npr.description: FIFA said Wednesday it had apologized for errors made over Gianni Infantino's failed plan to sell stakes in the World Cup and that senior staff in attendance at a crisis meeting in Morocco "reaffirmed their full support" for his presidency.

npr.title: Drone with explosives found at German airport, official sees 'new quality' of threat
npr.description: Regional police and prosecutors said an airport employee discovered a drone near the airport's south runway with "an unknown explosive device," and the object was examined by police

npr.title: Ousted Bangladeshi leader vows to return from exile despite facing a death sentence
npr.description: Hasina's speech marked the second anniversary of her ouster. She fled Bangladesh by helicopter following nearly two months of protests in 2024 that left nearly 1,400 people dead, according to the United Nations.

republika.title: Caldo record, il rifugio lombardo più alto costretto a chiudere: “Rischio frane, troppo pericoloso”
republika.description: La struttura ricettiva, il “Rifugio Marco e Rosa” sul Bernina, si trova a 3609 metri di quota: tra i 2800 e i tremila, si sono aperte voragini nella neve e nel ghiaccio. Il gestore: “Rischio cedimenti, mai successo nulla di simile”

republika.title: Schengen, Madrid non ci sta: “Roma riapra lo spazio entro il 9, altrimenti misure proporzionali”
republika.description: La decisione secondo il governo Sánchez è stata presa in base a “motivazioni pretestuose non conformi né al Codice Frontiere né alla realtà dei fatti”. E in più si ricorda che Roma “dal 2022 non rispetta il Regolamento di Dublino”

republika.title: Cercava di entrare a Ceuta con il parapendio, morto un giovane
republika.description: Un migrante di origini subsahariane è precipitato in mare mentre cercava di raggiungere l’exclave. È il primo decesso in un tentativo di accesso via aerea

republika.title: Lite Bartolozzi-FI. Gli azzurri chiedono un’indagine sul carcere, e lei: “State all’opposizione?”
republika.description: Sui social la replica piccata dell’ex capa di gabinetto di Nordio al deputato Tommaso Calderone, critico sulla condizione degli istituti penitenziari

republika.title: Taddeucci bronzo nella 3 km knockout sprint agli Europei di nuoto
republika.description: L’azzurra sale ancora una volta sul podio dopo gli ori nella 10 e nella 5 km. Successo della tedesca Gose

republika.title: Kenya, Rift Valley allagata come non mai. Due laghi, salato e dolce, stanno per fondersi
republika.description: Il dramma nell’area che lambisce l’equatore, 200 km a Nord-ovest di Nairobi: case sommerse o comunque abbandonate da una popolazione costretta a vivere a tu per tu con coccodrilli e ippopotami; turismo in agonia. “Se il Lake Baringo e il Bogoria si congiungeranno, sarà disastro totale”

republika.title: Francesco Guccini, il nostro Bob Dylan. Con lui la rivoluzione sembrò a portata di mano
republika.description: Il primo album Folk beat n.1 sconvolse i ragazzi degli anni 60. La forza di Auschwitz e La locomotiva, glorioso pezzo da cantastorie

republika.title: Francesco Guccini, il gigante che ha trasformato le parole in memoria
republika.description: Con la sua lingua colta, l’antidivismo e le canzoni senza tempo, il cantautore modenese lascia un’eredità capace di unire generazioni

republika.title: Fabri Fibra: “Ho amato Guccini ascoltando “L’avvelenata”, cantava cose che gli altri non dicevano”
republika.description: Il rapper, protagonista lo scorso anno di un incontro molto speciale con il cantautore per la copertina de “Il Venerdì”, ricorda il “Maestrone”: “Con lui se ne va un’idea di artista che metteva al centro le canzoni, non sé stesso”

republika.title: Lo chiameremo Kvaracopia
republika.description: Tornike scoprirà presto quanto difficile possa essere farsi largo in un mondo dove un Kvara esiste già

republika.title: Carl Bildt: “Su Ceuta l’Europa ha reagito per paura di una crisi fuori controllo”
republika.description: L’ex primo ministro svedese: “La risposta probabilmente è stata eccessiva, ma dimostra quanto il tema sia sensibile in molti Paesi del Continente”

republika.title: ll Mediterraneo tocca 33 gradi, mai così calda l’acqua del mare: “L’aria fresca innescherà disastri”
republika.description: L’estate delle ondate di calore senza fine continua a stupire gli esperti: “Siamo circondati da una polveriera, l’arrivo delle correnti potrebbe scatenare fenomeni atmosferici violenti”

republika.title: Droni su obiettivi tedeschi in Ucraina. La pista russa per l’attacco a Lipsia
republika.description: Nel mirino una nave e un deposito di aziende legate alla Germania. I servizi denunciano: interferenze del Cremlino sulle elezioni

republika.title: L’esperto di antiterrorismo: “È stato un raid molto grave, riflettere se coinvolgere la Nato”
republika.description: Hans-Jakob Schindler, del Counter Extremism Project: “Se emergessero le prove che dietro ai droni in aeroporto c’è la mano di Mosca, ci sarebbero gli estremi per attivare l’articolo 4 dell’Alleanza”

republika.title: L’Iran chiude Hormuz agli Usa e punta a pedaggi da 100 miliardi
republika.description: Teheran provoca mentre è pronta l’intesa con l’Oman per far ripartire il traffico nello Stretto: “Ma non alle navi americane e israeliane”

republika.title: La sfuriata di Trump a Hegseth: “È tua la colpa degli arsenali vuoti”
republika.description: Secondo i media sarebbe avvenuta a Camp David, il segretario alla Guerra avrebbe dato la colpa al vice. La Casa Bianca smentisce

republika.title: Delmastro, chat oscurate. Tre ricorsi alla Consulta per l’accesso ai dialoghi
republika.description:
Dopo il no della Camera alla Procura, al lavoro i pm di Roma
  
  
   la difesa di Caroccia e il presidente della Giunta regolamento, Dori

republika.title: Costa: “Su Delmastro richiesta generica dai pm. Difendiamo i diritti, non i politici”
republika.description: Il capogruppo berlusconiano alla Camera: “Doveva esserci un incontro sulle proposte di FI ma il ministro Nordio lo ha rinviato. In Aula affermeremo le nostre idee sulla giustizia”. E tra le priorità indica carceri e risarcimenti

elpais.title: Última hora de la entrada de inmigrantes a Ceuta, en directo | El Gobierno da un ultimátum a Italia para que retire los controles en frontera a los viajeros procedentes de España
elpais.description: El Ejecutivo ha registrado ya a 1.342 menores en Ceuta: “Van a ser atendidos todos” | Marlaska, Albares, Robles y Bolaños comparecerán en el Congreso por la crisis en Ceuta

elpais.title: Pulso entre el Gobierno y el PP por las explicaciones parlamentarias sobre la crisis de Ceuta
elpais.description: Cuatro ministros comparecerán a partir del 25 en el Congreso e ignorarán el intento de los populares de anticipar las citas la próxima semana en el Senado

elpais.title: Las ONG de Marruecos elevan a 141 la cifra de muertos a ambos lados de la frontera de Ceuta
elpais.description: La Asociación Marroquí de Derechos Humanos recopila datos oficiales y de organizaciones humanitarias

elpais.title: El PSOE denuncia ante la justicia la compra del ático del Gobierno de Ayuso: “Se van a arrepentir”
elpais.description: Óscar López anuncia medidas legales contra el consejo de administración de Planifica Madrid para aclarar la adquisición por más de seis millones del inmueble de lujo

elpais.title: Planifica Madrid actualiza su agenda una vez que El País publica que la mantenía oculta desde el 26 de marzo
elpais.description: La empresa pública se dispone ahora a resolver el apagón informativo, aunque limita la información relativa a la compra del ático de Chamberí a la siguiente anotación: “FIRMA NOTARIA. 14:00. EXTERNA”

elpais.title: El control constante durante años del exguardia civil que mató a su expareja: llegó a denunciarla 45 veces solo “por joder”
elpais.description: Dámaso Fernández mató a Laura Cruz, dejando tres huérfanos, después de una última denuncia de su víctima y tras conocer que había sido expulsado del cuerpo

elpais.title: La policía que acusa de acoso sexual y laboral al comisario de La India rechaza que el juez tenga acceso a su móvil
elpais.description: La defensa de la agente le recuerda que ella es la víctima y que el comisario Emilio de la Calle no puso en cuestión en su declaración las grabaciones en las que se le escucha agredirla verbalmente

elpais.title: El giro de guion de Rodri: de la gran oferta del Madrid a elegir al Barça
elpais.description: El centrocampista del Manchester City se ha debatido entre los dos grandes del fútbol español después de conquistar el Mundial

elpais.title: Mojito, piscina y despido: el peligro del teletrabajo en verano fuera de tu residencia habitual
elpais.description: Esta práctica genera dudas entre los expertos en derecho laboral por el cumplimiento del contrato, los riesgos laborales y el deber de confidencialidad

elpais.title: Abstemio social
elpais.description: Yo lo que pienso es que ya llevo dos años y medio sin beber y que en algo se tenía que notar, y que esa frescura y esa agilidad mental son ahora las nuevas cadenas de mi identidad

elpais.title: ‘Blue Film’, la película sobre pederastia que incomoda a la industria: “El rechazo que genera tiene que ver con los traumas de quien mira”
elpais.description: El polémico debut del británico Elliot Tuttle, protagonizado por un joven trabajador sexual y su antiguo profesor de secundaria, se estrena este viernes en Filmin tras ser premiado en el Atlàntida Mallorca Film Fest

elpais.title: La guerra cultural se libra con el color: ¿por qué las superproducciones de Hollywood se han vuelto tan grises?
elpais.description: ‘La odisea’ es el último ejemplo de una gran superproducción que, frente al vibrante tecnicolor del pasado, apuesta por colores grises, oscuros y planos buscando una especie de paralelismo visual a los tiempos que vivimos

elpais.title: Primer parte de la Aemet para el eclipse: nubes en zonas de montaña del norte y el este de la Península
elpais.description: Un portavoz da un primer esbozo del tiempo que hará el día del fenómeno a la espera de la publicación de la predicción especial y advierte del riesgo de incendios

elpais.title: Tres Cantos cancela las actividades del eclipse solar y una plataforma pide que no se celebren en la Sierra Norte
elpais.description: Solo una treintena de municipios madrileños de los 52 previstos ha presentado un plan de emergencia y mantiene las actividades, según informa ASEM 112 al Sindicato de Bomberos

elpais.title: ¿Dónde y a qué hora ver el eclipse solar en España? El mapa definitivo para saber cómo será en cada municipio

hn.description:
Author here.

Background, for anyone who hasn't followed this fight: IBM's iron–sulfur SQD results (Sci. Adv. 2025) are one of the flagship "quantum computers are useful for chemistry now" claims, and a published critique (arXiv:2501.07231) argues the quantum samples never beat classical selected-CI at matched cost. That argument is still live.

Both sides have been arguing about energies. Neither measured which electronic state these calculations actually converge to.

So I measured it. ⟨

phys-org.description: If you ask Vijay Parashar, associate professor of medical and molecular sciences (MMSC) at the University of Delaware College of Health Sciences, human bodies are bags of bacteria. "It sounds gross, but not all bacteria are bad; most of them are good. The trouble starts when the bad bacteria learn how to outsmart antibiotics."

phys-org.title: An elegant modification doubles the range of low-noise 'white lasers' in a single fiber
phys-org.description: Supercontinuum light sources—often called "white lasers" because they emit a broad, continuous rainbow of colors—are essential tools for everything from advanced medical imaging to environmental gas detection. However, researchers have historically faced a frustrating trade-off: A broad spectrum comes at the expense of high fluctuations, which has effectively limited their use.

phys-org.title: Mushroom behind 'tiny people' hallucinations identified
phys-org.description: People in communities thousands of miles apart have described the same strange experience after eating a mysterious mushroom: vivid visions of tiny humans moving through and interacting with the physical world around them. Known as Lilliputian hallucinations—a reference to the 6-inch-tall inhabitants of "Gulliver's Travels"—the phenomenon has long been thought to stem from cultural influences rather than biology.

phys-org.title: Decoding the North American bison's genome to better inform conservation efforts
phys-org.description: A new study by ancient DNA researchers at the University of California, Santa Cruz, used paleogenomics to create a genetic roadmap to help guide the restoration of another iconic species once on the brink of extinction: the North American bison.

phys-org.title: Researchers demonstrate first fully solution-processed solid-state polariton laser
phys-org.description: Researchers have demonstrated a solid-state organic laser microcavity fabricated entirely by solution processing. The device operates in the strong light–matter coupling regime, where light and matter form hybrid states called polaritons. This makes the platform not only a new type of solution-processed laser but also a powerful way to study nonlinear polariton interactions. The paper is published in the journal Nature Communications.

phys-org.title: Never-before-seen woven structure that forms naturally inside a crystal discovered

phys-org.title: One-third of agricultural land accounts for two-thirds of global impact, study reveals

But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

proj-syn.title: Will Iceland Rejoin the EU Path?
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump’s volatile and unpredictable security policies, particularly his desire to control Greenland, have put Iceland in a vulnerable position. This uncomfortable reality will likely be front of mind as voters decide whether to reopen membership negotiations with the European Union.

proj-syn.title: Democracy, Autocracy, or Something Else?
proj-syn.description: Contrary to conventional wisdom, the world is neither converging on liberal democracy nor being swept by an authoritarian tide. The decisive political struggles of the 21st century will be won or lost through the unglamorous work of strengthening democratic accountability and building effective institutions.

proj-syn.title: Colombia’s New Right-Wing Government Faces an Uphill Battle
proj-syn.description: Colombian President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella inherits an economy constrained by weak investment and a severe fiscal crisis. His ability to restore fiscal stability without sacrificing the social gains of recent decades will determine whether the country’s rightward shift proves lasting or short-lived.

proj-syn.title: Can Progressives Deliver Economic Growth?
proj-syn.description: At a time of historic inequality and inadequate public investment, the kind of redistributive policies promoted by politicians on the left are badly needed. But given that no jurisdiction can tax and regulate its way to affordability, a growth-enhancing agenda that generates good jobs and productive capacity is also vital.

proj-syn.title: Fauci’s Modern Pillory
proj-syn.description: MAGA Republicans’ decision to drag Anthony Fauci before a Senate hearing was less about their hatred of science and more about their disdain for the scientists who guide lawmakers in their decision-making. They couldn’t wait to pillory him, and by association any public-facing expert, in front of the cameras.

proj-syn.title: Cheaper Mortgages Won’t Solve the US Housing Crisis
proj-syn.description: For decades, federal housing policy has favored cheaper financing over expanding the housing supply, despite evidence that expanding mortgage credit increases borrowing and house prices. The bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act marks an important shift by emphasizing measures that make it easier to build more homes.

proj-syn.title: The Right Way to Regulate AI
proj-syn.description: Governments tend to treat AI as a national-security challenge while devoting far less attention to its effects on education, health, labor markets, and the judiciary. Addressing AI’s societal risks requires institutions designed to recognize and respond to emerging threats before they become systemic failures.

proj-syn.title: Global Tax Reform Is the Key to a Fair AI Economy
proj-syn.description: The rise of AI has highlighted how the global tax system is ill-suited to capture the profits derived from such technology. While creating an equitable AI economy ultimately requires a durable and robust multilateral tax framework, digital-service taxes can serve as an important stepping stone to that outcome.

proj-syn.title: Aid’s Next Chapter
proj-syn.description: Wars, epidemics, displacement, and geopolitical competition will ensure that rich countries continue to spend money abroad, whether for humanitarian reasons or in pursuit of their own interests. The only question is what sort of aid system will emerge from the current retrenchment.

proj-syn.title: Peace With Iran Won’t Last Unless It Benefits Ordinary Iranians
proj-syn.description: A sustainable peace agreement between the United States and Iran will require more than military deterrence. Without financial sanctions relief that fuels job creation and generates real economic opportunities for ordinary Iranians, it will likely suffer the same fate as the 2015 nuclear deal.

proj-syn.title: Why Wealth Taxes Always Fail
proj-syn.description: A clear-eyed view of past experience shows that where wealth taxes have been tried, they have usually been abandoned—and for good reason. As policymakers in California, New York, France, and elsewhere revisit this old idea, they should heed the lessons of this history.

proj-syn.title: A New Paradigm for Global Health Financing
proj-syn.description: As aid flows decline, more countries are articulating a new vision in which health financing would build on national resources, answer to domestic priorities, and remain accountable to their own citizens. Such a change is long overdue, and it can be achieved by pursuing reforms in three areas.

proj-syn.title: The Triumph of India’s Cockroaches
proj-syn.description: The concessions secured by the "cockroach movement" amount to more than a triumph for prospective medical students or a brief political headache for the country's ruling party. They prove that even after years of centralization and institutional erosion, power remains with the people.

proj-syn.title: Zombie Monetarism
proj-syn.description: Three prominent economists, including a former Federal Reserve governor and adviser to US President Donald Trump, have just endorsed “soft monetarism” as a way to guide the Fed's approach to inflation. But the "quantity theory" of money failed for good reasons, and those reasons have not changed.

proj-syn.title: Taiwan Needs a New Deterrence Strategy
proj-syn.description: Emboldened by US President Donald Trump’s war in Iran, Chinese leaders have ramped up their gray-zone coercion against Taiwan in recent months. To avert a Chinese invasion, Taiwan must ensure that other democracies cannot function without it by providing them with more than just semiconductors.

proj-syn.title: What a Sino-American G2 Would Mean for Asian Security
proj-syn.description: The G2 concept that Donald Trump has lately been touting is a highly unstable proposition, which could make the emergence of a unipolar Asia more likely. Fortunately, Japan remains committed to advancing the far more effective “free and open Indo-Pacific” framework, with India as an indispensable partner.

proj-syn.title: Tearing Down the Currency Wall
proj-syn.description: Most of the world seems to misunderstand why global capital is not financing the developing world’s climate transition. The real problem lies in the structure of price formation, which policymakers can best address by focusing on three key priorities.

proj-syn.title: The Case for a Pay-Where-You-Play Tax System
proj-syn.description: The global tax system has repeatedly put corporate interests ahead of people and the planet by allowing multinationals to transfer profits to tax havens. If adopted, the proposed UN Framework Convention on International Tax Cooperation would overturn the century-old rules that make this possible.
